subject: mud volcano
title: What If a Mud Volcano Never Stopped? Indonesia's Has Run Since 2006

scenes.text: What if a mud volcano opened by your town and never stopped? Indonesia's hasn't since 2006.
On May 29th, 2006, hot mud and gas burst out of a rice field in East Java, near a gas drilling rig.
At its peak it pumped over 100,000 cubic meters of mud a day. Whole villages vanished under it.
More than 40,000 people lost their homes. Engineers built earth levees and simply let the mud lake grow inside them.
Scientists argued over the cause: an earthquake two days earlier, or the gas well, which lacked a protective casing.
Twenty years on it still flows. Models say until the late 2030s; the gas may seep for centuries.

description:
What if a mud volcano opened next to your town and never stopped? On 29 May 2006, hot mud began erupting from a rice field in Sidoarjo, East Java, near a gas exploration well. At its peak it produced well over 100,000 cubic meters of mud a day, burying more than a dozen villages and displacing over 40,000 people; the damage is estimated at nearly 3 billion dollars.
Scientists still debate whether an earthquake two days earlier or the drilling triggered it. Models suggest the flow will continue until the late 2030s.
What should we run through next?
thumbnail_text: WHAT IF THE MUD NEVER STOPPED?
first_comment: Satellites still photograph the mud lake from orbit; the fresh mud shows up dark brown and the dried crust pale. Would you stay in a town next to it, and what should we run through next?
